name: Spokeo
notes: First search your name on spokeo.com and open your actual listing — the opt-out form needs that specific profile URL (e.g. spokeo.com/Smith-Sample/Houston/TX/p12345678), not just your email.

name: BeenVerified
notes: Cloudflare human-verification check often appears before the form loads — just complete it.

name: PeopleFinders
notes: Don't search yourself via their main search bar — that's their paid-report sales funnel ("View Details" tries to sell you a report, no opt-out there). Use this link instead: click Next, enter name+email, click the confirmation link they email you, then fill out the actual removal form. They explicitly say new public records can re-add you, so periodic rechecking (which this app already does) is expected. PublicRecordsNow appears to be an affiliate front-end with no data of its own, feeding searches here — this opt-out should cover that one too.

name: MyLife
notes: Known to be aggressive about re-listing; check carefully on recheck. Page can render blank on first load (Cloudflare bot-check) — reload if that happens.

name: Radaris
notes: Dead/defunct (Oct 2026): a NJ court seized this domain (and Rehold.com, Trustoria.com) from its operators under Daniel's Law and permanently barred them from disclosing personal info. No opt-out needed — they're legally barred from operating as a people-search site. Safe to mark not found.

name: PublicRecordsNow
notes: PublicRecordsNow looks like it's been rebuilt as a lead-gen front page with no database of its own (Oct 2026) — its search sends you to peoplefinders.com with affiliate tracking params, and its own /optout/ page no longer works (just falls through to its homepage). Opting out via PeopleFinders (which this link now points to directly) should cover this one too — nothing separate to do here.

name: Nuwber
notes: nuwber.com itself appears to be down (confirmed dead as of Oct 2026). Nuwber Inc. is still an active registered data broker though — email support@nuwber.com directly to request opt-out/deletion, or call (844) 912-1292. Clicking the broker name opens your mail client with a pre-filled CCPA request — just fill in your name/city/state. Worth rechecking occasionally in case the site comes back.

name: PeekYou
notes: Dead/defunct (Oct 2026): domain was handed over to Atlas Data Privacy Corp as part of a NJ "Daniel's Law" lawsuit settlement; the site no longer operates as a people-search engine. No opt-out needed. Safe to mark not found.

name: FamilyTreeNow
notes: URL is correct even though it looks like a search form — per their own FAQ, you locate your record, confirm by email, then an opt-out action appears for that record. Often sits behind a Cloudflare "verify you're human" check first.

name: AdvancedBackgroundChecks
notes: Page is titled "opt out of sale and sharing" (CCPA legal wording) and doesn't obviously say "remove me" — it's the real removal flow anyway. Enter name+email, click the confirmation link they email you, then fill out the actual opt-out form that opens. Can take up to 45 days to fully process (slower than most of these).
